text:
sam: heads up — I want to propose we move ownership of the adaptive throttle circuit (the part that applies graduated penalties during surges) from eng-platform to eng-infra. There are infra-only concerns (kernel-level backpressure, qdisc interactions) that keep coming up in rollouts.
julia: curious — what's the minimum surface area eng-platform would still own?
sam: short answer: policy config and the admission predicates. eng-infra would own the runtime circuit, penalty execution, telemetry, and graceful fail-open logic.
arjun: +1 to splitting runtime vs policy. wondering about the contract shape though — a small set of RPCs? webhooks?
sam: envisioned contract: 1) EvaluateAdmission(request_meta) -> {allow|defer|penalize, reason_code} 2) ReportOutcome(request_id, outcome_metrics) 3) SubscribeTelemetry(stream_selector) -> continuous metrics. Keep it language-agnostic (gRPC over mTLS).
eva: need to call out SLIs: percent-deferred, mean-penalty-duration, rollback-rate. Also important: a bounded time budget for EvaluateAdmission (<2ms p95).
arjun: can we embed a small policy shim in platform that keeps EvaluateAdmission local for simple rules and falls back to infra for heavy scoring? avoids network hop on common fast-paths.
sam: yes — a local predicate cache is fine. key requirement: semantics must be identical so cached results don't diverge. We'll have a policy fingerprint/version in the contract so mismatch rejects local cache.
julia: telemetry ownership note: infra should push raw penalty events to bigquery and also to the policy team via a realtime topic so we can correlate eval inputs -> outcomes for regressions.
infra-bot: deploy-note: adaptive-throttle-v2 will be flagged for staged rollout. Canary group=10% for zone-a, ramp steps=10, rollback on penalty-rate > 1% increase.
eva: question about penalty windows: current design uses sliding windows with exponential decay. That couples with admission budget math. If infra owns execution we need to expose window parameters in the policy API, otherwise ops can't reason about unit economics.
sam: agree — make window params first-class in the policy config (decay_half_life, max_accumulator). Platform policy UI can show cost impact estimates.
arjun: failure modes: 1) infra network partition -> should fail open with conservative grace quota and emit high-priority alerts. 2) policy mismatch -> reject local cache and fallback to infra; if infra unavailable, fall back to simplest token-bucket with low rate. Documented in runbook.
julia: ops checklist: - flaggable feature gate - metrics dashboard (penalty_applied, deprioritized_tenants) - alert thresholds - automated rollback lambda
eva: can we add a small example config snippet for the policy UI?
sam: sure: 
```
policy_version: "2026-02-01"
rules:
  - id: surge_penalty_v1
    matcher: tenant_score > 0.8
    action: penalize
    penalty:
      decay_half_life: 30s
      max_accumulator: 1000
      step_ms: 200
```
arjun: thanks — last ask: include ownership for canary playbook (who flips canaries, who monitors). my vote: eng-platform owns canary gating and user-visible rollout; eng-infra owns the underlying circuit and rollback trigger hooks.
sam: agreed. I'll write a short RFC follow-up summarizing boundaries + runbooks. Will link the canary checklist and the initial telemetry dashboards. Anyone wanna co-author?
julia: I'll take telemetry dashboards.
eva: I'll help write the rollback triggers section.
arjun: I'll draft the RPC schema and the security model (mTLS + per-team auth).
infra-bot: action-created: RFC-6167890001-adaptive-throttle-handoff assigned -> sam, julia, arjun, eva. Due: 2026-03-05.
sam: thanks all. quick sync tomorrow 11am to lock the contract.
